concepts.title: Animal Husbandry: Dairy, Poultry, and Fisheries

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Animal Husbandry: Dairy, Poultry, and Fisheries' refers to.
questions.a: The agricultural practice of breeding and raising livestock including cattle for dairy, birds for poultry, and aquatic organisms for fisheries to meet the growing demand for food of animal origin.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Animal Husbandry: Dairy, Poultry, and Fisheries'.
questions.a: Animal husbandry encompasses dairy farming, poultry management, and fisheries to enhance production of milk, eggs, meat, and fish for human consumption.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Animal Husbandry: Dairy, Poultry, and Fisheries'.
questions.a: define animal husbandry and list its major branches

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Animal Breeding: Inbreeding and Outbreeding' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic mating of animals to increase yield and develop desirable traits, encompassing inbreeding (mating of related animals) and outbreeding (mating of unrelated animals).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Animal Breeding: Inbreeding and Outbreeding'.
questions.a: Inbreeding increases homozygosity and can cause inbreeding depression, while outbreeding including crossbreeding introduces hybrid vigour and improves productivity.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Animal Breeding: Inbreeding and Outbreeding'.
questions.a: differentiate between inbreeding and outbreeding in animal breeding

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Bee-Keeping (Apiculture)' refers to.
questions.a: The practice of rearing honey bees for the production of honey and beeswax, requiring knowledge of bee behaviour, colony structure, and suitable pasturage.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bee-Keeping (Apiculture)'.
questions.a: Apiculture yields honey, a highly nutritious food, and beeswax, while requiring suitable bee species, pasturage, and colony management.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Bee-Keeping (Apiculture)'.
questions.a: what is apiculture and why is it important

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Plant Breeding: Steps and Methods' refers to.
questions.a: The purposeful manipulation of plant species to create improved crop varieties with higher yield, better quality, and resistance to diseases through a defined sequence of steps.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Plant Breeding: Steps and Methods'.
questions.a: Plant breeding follows four steps: collection of variability, evaluation and selection of parents, cross hybridisation of selected parents, and testing and commercial release of new cultivars.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Plant Breeding: Steps and Methods'.
questions.a: list the main steps of plant breeding

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Tissue Culture and Micropropagation' refers to.
questions.a: The technique of regenerating whole plants from explant tissues or single cells grown on nutrient medium under aseptic conditions, exploiting the totipotency of plant cells.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Tissue Culture and Micropropagation'.
questions.a: Micropropagation allows rapid production of disease-free, genetically identical plants, while somaclonal variation generates useful genetic diversity in culture.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Tissue Culture and Micropropagation'.
questions.a: what is tissue culture and on what property of cells is it based

questions.q: Using the method 'Single Cell Protein (SCP)', work with: conversion_efficiency = 10, protein_content_percent = 20, substrate_mass = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of protein_yield.
questions.a: 24 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Single Cell Protein (SCP)' and work with: conversion_efficiency = 25, protein_content_percent = 25, substrate_mass = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of protein_yield.
questions.a: 50 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Single Cell Protein (SCP)' refers to.
questions.a: The production of protein-rich biomass from unicellular microorganisms such as algae, fungi, bacteria, and yeast grown on inexpensive substrates for use as food or feed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Single Cell Protein (SCP)'.
questions.a: Single cell protein provides an alternative protein source by cultivating microbes on waste materials, reducing pressure on conventional agriculture.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Single Cell Protein (SCP)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: protein_yield = microbial_biomass * protein_fraction

questions.q: Using the method 'Biofortification: Enhancing Nutritional Quality', work with: fortified_level = 360, original_level = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of nutrient_increase_percent.
questions.a: 200 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Biofortification: Enhancing Nutritional Quality' and work with: fortified_level = 100, original_level = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of nutrient_increase_percent.
questions.a: 1150 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biofortification: Enhancing Nutritional Quality' refers to.
questions.a: The breeding strategy of developing crop varieties with higher levels of vitamins, minerals, and proteins to improve the nutritional quality of food.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biofortification: Enhancing Nutritional Quality'.
questions.a: Biofortification enriches crops with micronutrients and essential amino acids, addressing hidden hunger caused by nutrient-deficient diets.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Biofortification: Enhancing Nutritional Quality', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: nutrient_increase_percent = ((fortified_level - original_level) / original_level) * 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Green Revolution and Plant Breeding' refers to.
questions.a: The dramatic increase in crop production achieved through the development and adoption of high-yielding, disease-resistant semi-dwarf varieties of wheat and rice during the mid-twentieth century.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Green Revolution and Plant Breeding'.
questions.a: The Green Revolution relied on plant breeding to produce semi-dwarf varieties of wheat and rice that responded to fertilizers and reduced lodging, dramatically increasing food grain production.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Green Revolution and Plant Breeding'.
questions.a: what was the green revolution and which crops were involved
